sources.entry: Mudroom - Open-source app and CLI that runs coding agents like Claude Code and Codex in a Linux micro-VM on a copy-on-write clone of your project, then lets you review and apply their changes like a pull request. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Kernel-Hunter/mudroom) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: Mudroom is a free, MIT-licensed app and CLI that runs coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, opencode, Aider, or any command) on a copy-on-write clone of your project inside a Linux micro-VM or container, with allowlisted network access, and lets you review and selectively apply their changes.
use_cases: Run Claude Code or Codex on a project without letting it touch your real folder
Review and selectively apply AI agent edits file by file or hunk by hunk
Restrict which hosts an AI agent can reach and log its connections
Keep .env files and keys out of an agent's working copy
Run local models via Ollama or LM Studio inside a sandboxed agent session
Undo changes an agent made to a project
notable: Your project folder is never mounted; the agent edits a copy-on-write clone and changes apply only when you choose
Locked-by-default network allowlist via a local proxy that logs every connection and the program that opened it
Per-file and per-hunk review with undo for each apply, and your own concurrent edits are never overwritten
Keeps .env, *.pem, SSH keys and .netrc out of the agent's copy by default, configurable with .gitignore-style patterns
Works as a macOS app and a CLI on macOS, Linux and Windows (review app is macOS only)
caveats: Early prototype; expect rough edges and breaking changes
The Mac review app requires Apple silicon and macOS 26; Linux, Windows and Intel Macs get CLI only, using Docker or Podman
Mac app is ad-hoc signed, not notarized, so Gatekeeper needs manual approval when downloaded in a browser
